findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a person merges a ready pull request after sign-off while its native builder still has a pending handback.
The new release event is recorded by `forge merge`, which refuses when the repo uses the default human-merge setting (`src/forge/merge.py:49-50`). `forge close` recognizes the merged pull request and returns without recording that event (`src/forge/close.py:185-194`), so the surviving session keeps the builder place and waiting work remains blocked. The new merge tests force `merge = "agent"` for both clients (`tests/test_finished_builds_free_places.py:37`).

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a ready pull request merges while its builder result is awaiting handback, and local files cause Forge to retain the worktree.
Removing the entry makes `native.handback` treat that pending round as stopped or replaced (`src/forge/native.py:224-226`). It refuses before recording the builder's result or reaching the pending-record and lock cleanup at lines 239-243. The coordinator therefore cannot hand back the result or receive a commit nudge for the retained work, and the item lock remains held.
findings.title: Keep a pending handback usable after a merge frees its place

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a finished builder asks a question and handback publishes it to GitHub.
The test waits for `handback` to return before checking admission. The existing `finally` in `src/forge/native.py:239-243` already releases the entry, so this case still passes if the new release on `run end` is removed. That misses the promised timing: `src/forge/native.py:293-298` records the end before the GitHub publication, which can keep handback running. The proof needs to observe waiting work start after the end is recorded and before handback returns.
findings.title: Gate: round completion releases capacity before handback returns

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a story part such as `BOARD/HELP` finishes or merges while another part waits for a builder place.
Every new case starts fixes for both the holder and the waiter; none exercises a story-part identity or starts a waiting part. A release regression that mishandles the slash in `BOARD/HELP` would therefore pass these cases while leaving that part's place occupied. The existing task handback test checks cleanup after handback returns (`tests/test_tools_native_work.py:150-155`), rather than admission after a recorded completion or merge.
findings.title: Gate: a waiting story part starts when capacity is released

why: A finished builder round can keep its builder place when the coordinator session stays alive, so other parts wait (issue 1429)
